the adoption of IT investment in the banking industry has two effects.
the network effects in banking services can be negative, and the negative effects are more pronounced in the early stage of IT adoption, which can explain the Solow Paradoxs.

the impact of information technology in the banking industry.
the effects of IT on the banking industry in two aspects.
the impact of information technology (it) on the banking industry in terms of the effects of it adoption and diffusion on the bank performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IT investment in banking industry has a negative effect in the short run and positive effect in the long run.
IT investment in the US banking system does not have a clear effect on the bank performance.
IT investment has both positive and negative impacts on bank performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IT investment in the banking industry is not a panacea for improving the performance of banks, as it is believed by many.
the network effects of IT investment are negative in the US banking sector, and the cost effects of IT investment have not been significant in the past 20 years.
IT investment is beneficial in terms of cost saving, but not necessarily in terms of increasing bank profits, which is consistent with the results of other studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of IT investment are not only positive or negative, but can also depend on the type of IT investment.
, the network effects of IT investment can be positive or negative, and it is the relative magnitude of the two effects that determines the overall impact of IT investment on bank performance.
IT adoption and diffusion may have different effects on banks’ profits.
